articles.title: 430,000-Year-Old Wooden Tools Rewrite the Story of Early Human Ingenuity
articles.summary: Archaeologists in Greece have unearthed the oldest known wooden tools, dating back 430,000 years—beating the previous record by 40,000 years. The finds include a digging stick and a carved fragment, revealing surprising skill in early humans. Even a bear’s claw marks were found nearby.

articles.title: Behind Every NASA Flight: The Unsung Heroes Keeping Experimental Aircraft Mission-Ready
articles.summary: At NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center, maintenance crews work tirelessly to keep a diverse fleet—from F-15s to the X-59—safe and operational. They handle everything from ejection seats to rapid reconfigurations, ensuring science missions never miss a beat. Crew chief Jose Rodriguez says they “adapt and overcome” any challenge.

articles.title: Can You Trust That Medical App? IEEE’s New Registry Aims to Separate Science from Hype
articles.summary: Over 55,000 therapeutic apps claim to treat conditions like depression or diabetes, but most lack independent review. IEEE’s new Global Medical Mobile App Assessment and Registry will verify apps for clinical efficacy, ethical design, and data security, helping patients and doctors spot trustworthy tools.
